learningObjective: Diagnose why per-tensor MinMax INT8 activation quantization collapses accuracy on a Transformer layer with heavy-tail activation outliers.
profileData:
Per-tensor INT8 quantization of LLM linear layer input activations:
  Activation distribution: ~99% of values within [-2, 2]; ~1% of values in [-50, 50] (channel-localized outliers).
  MinMax calibration: threshold = 50 → scale s = 50 / 127 ≈ 0.394 → ~99% of values occupy only ~2 / 0.394 ≈ 5 out of 254 quantization levels.
  Observed effect: post-quantization perplexity increases 3-5×.
stem: Per-tensor MinMax INT8 quantization on this LLM layer collapses accuracy. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.text: Outliers force the per-tensor MinMax scale to be dominated by rare extremes, leaving only ~5 quantization levels for the 99% of activations in [-2, 2]; the resulting resolution is inadequate. Per-channel activation quantization or techniques like SmoothQuant that shift the outlier magnitude to the weights address this.
INT8 GEMM is mathematically incapable of representing LLM activations; only FP16 works.
The issue is a bug in the calibration code; a correct MinMax implementation would automatically handle outliers.
Per-tensor MinMax is the recommended calibration for LLMs; the perplexity increase reflects an inherent property of LLM output distributions and is unrelated to outlier handling.

explanation: The scenario captures the classical LLM outlier problem (documented in LLM.int8, SmoothQuant, AWQ): a small fraction of activation channels have magnitudes far exceeding the bulk distribution, driving the per-tensor MinMax scale up and wasting quantization levels. The fix is granularity refinement (per-channel activation quantization is often infeasible for post-attention activations, but per-token or per-channel-weight + activation-migration strategies work), or algorithmic techniques like SmoothQuant that migrate the outlier magnitude to weights (which can be per-channel-quantized). Options B, C, D are misdirection or misdiagnosis.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: standard outlier-driven MinMax failure and standard mitigations.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: INT8 GEMM works for LLMs with appropriate calibration.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: correct MinMax implementation still fails on outliers; the problem is the method, not the code.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: MinMax is not recommended for outlier-heavy activation distributions.

assumptions: The activation distribution matches the reported profile (99% narrow, 1% wide outliers in specific channels).
Symmetric per-tensor quantization with MinMax calibration.
nonImplications: Does not imply per-channel activation quantization is always feasible — some architectures make it hard to align activation channels across ops.
Does not imply SmoothQuant is the only remedy — AWQ, LLM.int8's mixed-precision fallback, and other methods exist.

distractorRationales.C: Blames implementation for a methodological limit.

sourceRefs.locator: Section on outlier characterization and migration

performanceClaim.scope: Per-tensor INT8 MinMax failure on outlier-heavy LLM activations
